result.situation: CASE-1042: Dupixent for adult atopic dermatitis, Northwind Commercial. Denied 2026-10-14 for ST-DOC (no step-therapy chart notes). This was the first submission. Chart notes with both trials arrived 2026-10-17 but have not been resubmitted. 615 hours remain in the window.

criteria.evidence: IGA 3 and BSA 18% on the PA form, repeated in the 06/30/2026 chart note.

criteria.criterion: Prescriber is a dermatologist, allergist or immunologist
Step 3a: medium-to-super-high-potency TCS for ≥28 consecutive days, with drug, dates and outcome
criteria.evidence: Triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID, 03/02 to 04/20/2026 (7 weeks), minimal improvement, IGA 3. The chart does not state a potency class; the payer applies its own classification.

criteria.criterion: Step 3b: TCI (tacrolimus or pimecrolimus) for ≥28 consecutive days, with drug, dates and outcome
criteria.evidence: Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment BID, started 04/21/2026, about 10 weeks at the 06/30 follow-up, inadequate response. Mild burning was noted but tolerated.

criteria.criterion: No concurrent biologic or JAK inhibitor for AD
criteria.evidence: PA form states no concurrent biologic or JAK inhibitor.

conflicts.description: Tacrolimus start appears as 04/20 (the start order) and 04/21 (confirmed actual start).
conflicts.resolution: Not a real conflict. The same provider record confirms the actual start was 04/21, and either date gives well over 28 days.

missing_information.why_it_matters: The policy requires a medium-to-super-high-potency TCS, and the chart names only the drug and strength.
missing_information.how_to_get: Not needed to resubmit. If the payer questions it, ask Riverside Dermatology for a clarifying note.

E1.reason: No contraindication or intolerance call is needed. Both steps are met by documented inadequate response in DOC-1042-02, and the burning was tolerated.

E2.reason: DOC-1042-01 and DOC-1042-02 agree on the trials, diagnosis and scores. NOTE-1 and NOTE-2 are consistent with them.

E3.reason: MSG-1 and MSG-2 concern only a fax cover sheet, not payer criteria. POLICY's last bulletin made no changes.

E4.reason: 615 hours remain per system facts and CASE, well over 48 hours, and we hold the needed docs (DOC-1042-02).

E5.reason: This is the first denial (submission_count 1 in CASE), so no peer-to-peer is needed.

E6.reason: No safety concern in DOC-1042-02 or any other source. Mild burning on tacrolimus was tolerated.

result.action_rationale: ST-DOC maps to RESUBMIT_WITH_DOCS when we hold the docs. DOC-1042-02 documents both required trials with drug, dates or duration, and outcome. All other criteria are met, no trigger fires, and the 30-day resubmission window is open.
parallel_actions: Log the resubmission and criteria checklist in CASE-1042 notes.
Use the June Northwind fax cover sheet per MSG-2, after a quick check that it is current.
could_not_determine: Whether Northwind classifies triamcinolone 0.1% cream as medium potency or higher; the chart does not state potency.
needs_human_judgment: Confirm that DOC-1042-02 is legible and complete before attaching it.

draft.to: Northwind Health Plan – Pharmacy Prior Authorization
draft.subject: PA Resubmission – Dupixent (dupilumab) – Ref CASE-1042 / Pt PT-58213 – Denial 2026-10-14 (ST-DOC)
draft.body:
We are resubmitting the prior authorization for Dupixent (dupilumab) 300 mg q2w for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (L20.9) under policy NW-RX-2207. This responds to the 2026-10-14 denial for missing step-therapy documentation.

Prescriber: Dr. Alana Reyes, Dermatology, Riverside Dermatology Associates.

The attached chart notes document:
- Topical corticosteroid: triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID, 03/02/2026 to 04/20/2026 (7 weeks). Minimal improvement, IGA 3. Discontinued.
- Topical calcineurin inhibitor: tacrolimus 0.1% ointment BID, started 04/21/2026, about 10 weeks as of 06/30/2026. Inadequate response.
- Severity on 06/30/2026: IGA 3, BSA 18%.
- No concurrent biologic or JAK inhibitor.

Please review for initial 6-month authorization.

Attachments: original PA request form; chart notes from Riverside Dermatology Associates.

Forus Access Operations
